Interpretation with Beige Book and SLOOS overlay

- Policy stance: The FOMC held the target range at 5.25–5.50% and kept balance sheet runoff on pace (Treasury cap $60B/month; agency MBS cap $35B). IORB at 5.4% and ON RRP at 5.3% remain the main operating tools. Cuts require “greater confidence” that inflation is moving sustainably to 2%.
- Statement macro tone: Real activity is solid, job gains strong, and inflation has eased but remains elevated. Risks to employment and inflation are moving toward better balance, with the Committee highly attentive to inflation risks.

Beige Book overlay
- Economic activity increased since January across districts, indicating continued growth momentum.
- Labor availability improved and wage pressures eased, signaling supply-side healing that should help disinflation.
- Businesses, including restauranteurs, are absorbing some price pressures, consistent with slower pass-through and margin compression.
- Inflation reports across districts point to moderating price growth, though not yet back to target.
- Ongoing stress in office-related CRE (e.g., New York) underscores sector-specific weakness.

SLOOS-informed credit conditions
- Weaker demand for C&I loans and tighter standards for CRE loans (including at foreign banks).
- Tighter standards across non-GSE/QM mortgage segments; GSE-eligible broadly unchanged.
- Auto loan standards tightened, constraining household credit.
- Tightening driven by outlook, risk, and liquidity/capital considerations.

Implications for policy tone
- Beige Book signals easing wage/price pressures and better labor supply, while SLOOS shows restrictive credit and soft loan demand—both are headwinds to growth and inflation.
- This combination tempers the cautiously hawkish statement, reducing the need for additional tightening and supporting patience while awaiting clearer, sustained disinflation.
- Net read: balanced to slightly dovish versus a statement-only read.
